repos/trade-imports-address-book, read on main (in step with origin/main): a Java 21 / Spring Boot REST service, the INS system of record for an organisation's Standard Address Block records and, since ruling:ian-2026-11-06, its transporters. No views or copy: its behaviour is an HTTP API under /organisation/{orgId}, documented in README.md (395 lines, the API overview, role rules, transporters, soft delete, expiry, indexes and design notes sections), docs/openapi/addresses.yml (1,024 lines, springdoc-generated, 10 operations: addresses and transporters each with list, create, get, replace and soft delete) and docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (890 lines, the human-authored locked contract). Code is in src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook (about 4,700 lines across 95 files): address/ (21 files, about 1,400 lines: the record, request and response, roles and role groups, the role validators, controller, service, list query), transporter/ (19 files, about 1,300 lines: the transporter record, private-or-commercial type, approval number and Northern Ireland country rules, controller, service, list query), top-level shared list and scoping classes (OrganisationScope, OrganisationScopedListQuery, ListMatchCriteria, ListPaging, SearchTerms, RequestedListFilterSupport, ExpiryIndexes, ClassLevelViolations), filter/IdentityHeaderFilter (the organisation header trust boundary), exceptions/ (the problem+json error shapes), and infrastructure (metrics/, configuration/ incl. tls/, logging/). Tests in src/test (about 9,800 lines): unit tests beside each package and 27 Testcontainers ITs in integration/. The repo keeps no rulings or decisions ledger: the only judgement-like documents are docs/review/EUDPA-58-review.md and its items JSON, a historical code review of the first build, not rulings. The source's scope is the address record: fields, types or usages (now roles), validation, organisation scoping and the API, so the extract covers address/, the shared list, paging, search and scoping classes, the identity filter, the error shapes, the expiry rules, the OpenAPI contract, the transporter record and API (the address book's other record, which the transporter-management blocked area and ruling:ian-2026-11-06 both turn on), and the tests that prove each. Left out: metrics/, configuration/ other than AddressTtlConfig, MongoConfig and OpenApiConfig, configuration/tls/, logging/, filter/HealthCheckFilter and RequestTracingFilter, application YAML beyond the TTL and environment settings, compose/, docker/, Dockerfile, pom.xml, .github/ workflows, .claude/, sonar config, and docs/review/ (2,660 lines of code-review history, no requirement or ruling).

Extracted in 5 parts:
Part 1, Address record, roles and request validation: Part 1, the address record, roles and request validation. Read in full: address/Address.java (the stored Mongo document, 69 lines), AddressRequest.java (the create and replace body with every Bean Validation constraint and message), AddressResponse.java (the wire shape and its null guards), AddressStatus.java (ACTIVE / DELETED tombstone), AddressRole.java (5 roles, each with its group and OpenAPI description), RoleGroup.java (SENDING, RECEIVING), RolesHeldTogether.java and its validator (the one-group class-level rule), AddressRoleNames.java and its validator (role names must be known enum names), AddressMapper.java (MapStruct: toResponse, toEntity, updateEntity), the shared ClassLevelViolations.java (keys a class-level violation to a property), the unit tests AddressRequestValidationTest (26 invalid-field cases, 8 at-maximum cases, the country, role-combination, unknown-role, repeat-collapse and free-phone tests), AddressMapperTest (8 tests), AddressResponseTest (3 tests), and the helpers AddressTestSupport, RecordNullGuards and ValidatorSupport; plus README.md's 'API overview' wire conventions and create example, 'Role rules', and the 'Design notes' bullets on AddressResponse, AddressRequest, @AddressRoleNames, @RolesHeldTogether and AddressMapper. Covered: every stored field and whether it is on the wire, every request field's constraints and messages verbatim, the 5 roles and 2 groups, the one-group rule, unknown, lower-case, null and blank role names, repeat collapse, the stray type and role fields, addressType, country being unrestricted and presence-only, the response fields with deleted and no status, the response null guards, and what create and update map. Two places where README and code differ are recorded as separate claims, not settled: README says countryCode is a 2-character ISO code, but the request only requires it to be non-blank and a test accepts a 50-character value; README says an addressType is ignored, while the request rejects fields named type and role.
Part 2, Address API: create, get, replace, soft delete and error shapes: Part 2 read, in full: address/AddressController.java (410 lines: list, create, get, update and delete handlers with their springdoc annotations; only create, get, update and delete are claimed here) and address/AddressService.java (197 lines: list, create with expiry stamping, get, update, soft delete; list left to part 3); the problem+json layer in exceptions/ (Problem, ValidationProblem, BadRequestException, NotFoundException, GlobalExceptionHandler, 277 lines together); the tests AddressServiceTest (616 lines, its create, get, update and delete tests claimed, its list tests left to part 3), GlobalExceptionHandlerTest (312 lines), IntegrationBase (459 lines, the shared IT helpers, including the bad-request matcher), AddressCrudIT (286 lines), AddressGetIT (64), AddressUpdateIT (232), AddressDeleteIT (142) and AddressTimingIT (61); docs/openapi/addresses.yml for POST /organisation/{orgId}/addresses and GET, PUT and DELETE /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{address-id} with the ValidationProblem, Problem, AddressRequest and AddressResponse components; and README.md sections 'API overview', 'Soft delete (tombstones)' and 'Design notes'. It covers the four single-address operations (method, path, body, status and response), soft delete and tombstones, what a 404 means, the 409 conflict and optimistic locking, every problem+json shape (validation-error, bad-request, not-found, conflict, internal-error) with type, title and detail strings, the traceId extension and the absence of instance, validation logging by field name only, createdAt and modifiedAt on create, update and delete, the non-prod expiry stamp on create, and the change counters and per-operation timers. Field-level rules and messages of AddressRequest (part 1), the list endpoint, paging, search and organisation scoping (part 3) and transporters (part 4) are left to other parts; where a create or replace test proves a field rule, only its API outcome (400 validation problem, nothing saved or stored row untouched) is claimed here.
Part 3, Address list, search, paging, organisation scoping and expiry: Part 3, address list, search, paging, organisation scoping and expiry. Read in full: address/AddressController.java (list path claimed, plus the organisation check every operation runs), address/AddressService.java (list path and the create-time expiry stamp claimed), AddressRepository, AddressListQuery, AddressListQueryImpl, ListCriteria, RequestedListFilters, AddressPageResponse; the shared top-level classes OrganisationScope, OrganisationScopedListQuery, ListMatchCriteria, ListPaging, SearchTerms, RequestedListFilterSupport and ExpiryIndexes (claimed once here for addresses and transporters); configuration/AddressTtlConfig and MongoConfig; filter/IdentityHeaderFilter; src/main/resources/application.yml (TTL, environment and Mongo client settings); the tests ListCriteriaTest, ListMatchCriteriaTest, OrganisationScopeTest, ExpiryIndexesTest, PageTestSupport (a test helper, proves nothing), AddressTtlConfigTest, IdentityHeaderFilterTest, IntegrationBase (shared IT helpers, incl. the bad-request matcher and the index assertions), AddressListIT, AddressSearchIT, AddressScopingIT, AddressExpiryIT, AddressRepositoryIT, AddressIndexIT and MongoConfigIT; docs/openapi/addresses.yml get /organisation/{orgId}/addresses and AddressPageResponse and the security scheme; README sections Security and trust boundary, API overview (list parameters and wire conventions), Address expiry (non-prod only), Indexes, and the Design notes bullets in scope. To find what the slice references, Address.java's @CompoundIndex and GlobalExceptionHandler's BadRequestException and type-mismatch handlers were also grepped. Covered: the GET list endpoint (route, paging bounds and messages, response object, ordering, tombstone exclusion, page beyond last), the four filters (q fields and literal partial matching, countryCode, role, searchRole), how they combine (role ANDed, q/countryCode/searchRole ORed), filter tidying, unknown-role 400, the searchRole label design, the trusted organisation header (400s, 404, problem bodies verbatim, MDC, logging), the controller-level organisation check, organisation and ACTIVE scoping of every query in general terms, the trust boundary the service relies on, non-prod expiry (variables, defaults, both prod safeguards, start-up failures, TTL indexes on both collections, what the TTL monitor removes), the org_status_created index, and the Mongo client settings MongoConfig proves.
Part 4, Transporters: Part 4, Transporters. Read in full on main: the 19 files of src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/transporter/ (the Transporter record in the transporters collection, TransporterRequest and TransporterResponse, TransporterType, TransporterStatus, the TransporterApprovalRequirement and CommercialTransporterCountry class-level constraints and their validators, TransporterController with its five operations, TransporterService, TransporterMapper, the list query, criteria, requested filters, page response and repository); the 6 unit test files in src/test/.../transporter/ (TransporterRequestValidationTest, TransporterServiceTest, TransporterMapperTest, TransporterResponseTest, TransporterListCriteriaTest and the TransporterTestSupport fixtures); integration/IntegrationBase.java (the transporter helpers and fixture bodies only) and the five transporter ITs (TransporterCrudIT, TransporterDeleteIT, TransporterScopingIT, TransporterSearchIT, TransporterIndexIT); docs/openapi/addresses.yml for the two transporter paths and the TransporterRequest, TransporterType, TransporterResponse and TransporterPageResponse components plus the security scheme; README.md's intro, 'Transporters', the transporter sentences of 'Soft delete (tombstones)' and the 'MongoDB' collections line. Covered: the stored record and its fields, every request field with its constraint and verbatim message, the stray roles and role refusals, the two types, the approval number and Northern Ireland country rules, the response shape and its derived deleted flag, the five operations with method, path, status and body, list paging, order, q over 7 fields, countryCode, type and searchType filters and their 400s, soft delete and tombstones, organisation scoping, the org_status_created index, the non-prod expiry stamp, metrics and logging, and the tests that prove each (named in each claim's note). No pages or copy files: the copy here is API validation messages. Shared scoping, paging and search classes are part 3's; only how transporters use them is claimed here.
Part 5, Locked API contract: Part 5, Locked API contract. Read in full: docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (890 lines: info with the wire, identity, soft delete, search, pagination, country code, roles and list-by-role conventions; one server; two tags; a global Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id security requirement; 4 paths with 10 operations, addresses and transporters each with list, create, get, replace and soft delete; components with the apiKey security scheme and 10 schemas: AddressRole, AddressRequest, ValidationProblem, Problem, AddressResponse, AddressPageResponse, TransporterType, TransporterRequest, TransporterResponse, TransporterPageResponse), integration/ApiContractComplianceIT.java (442 lines, 15 tests), openapi/OpenApiArtifactGeneratorIT.java (69 lines, the opt-in regenerator), testsupport/ApiDocs.java (73 lines, fetch, render and locked-contract loading), configuration/OpenApiConfig.java and JacksonConfig.java, src/main/resources/application-local.yml, and README.md's 'OpenAPI contract' section, the Swagger UI line under 'Running the local stack', the 'Testing' section and the 'Design notes' bullets on springdoc's ObjectMapper and the anyOf 400. Covered: every path, method, operationId, parameter (name and location) and response code the locked contract names; the AddressRole and TransporterType enums and where they are used; the AddressRequest and TransporterRequest required lists, field length bounds and minItems on roles; the Problem and ValidationProblem shapes and the anyOf 400 on create and update; the page response shapes and page and pageSize bounds; what the build check compares and how the artifact is regenerated; that /v3/api-docs and Swagger UI are on only under the local profile; and the camelCase wire, unknown-property and date conventions. What each operation does is left to parts 2 to 4; the contract's info prose on those behaviours is claimed only as what the contract states.

claims.statement: An address is stored as a document in the MongoDB collection named addresses, owned by one organisation.
claims.quote:
/** An organisation-owned address-book entry. {@code roles} can be null or empty. */
@Document(collection = "addresses")

claims.statement: The stored address holds these fields: id, name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email (all strings), roles (a list of address roles), organisationId (string), status (ACTIVE or DELETED), createdAt, modifiedAt and expireAt (instants), and version (a number).
claims.note: The stored record has no address type field: roles replaced it.

claims.statement: A stored address's roles may be null or empty: the record itself does not require a role, only the request does.
claims.quote: {@code roles} can be null or empty.

claims.statement: The address's createdAt is set by the database auditing when it is first saved, and modifiedAt each time it is saved.
A stored address carries a version number, which inferred from the Spring Data @Version annotation gives optimistic locking: a save against a stale version is refused.
claims.quote:
@Version
  private Long version;
claims.note: mechanism: version counter on the stored address. How a conflict answers over HTTP is part 2's.

claims.statement: Addresses are indexed by organisation, then status, then newest created first (index org_status_created).
Two addresses are the same address when their ids are equal, whatever their other fields hold.
claims.note: mechanism: identity of the stored address.

claims.statement: An address's status is ACTIVE or DELETED; DELETED is a soft-delete tombstone that is left out of lists but can still be read by id.
claims.quote:
Soft-delete tombstone status. {@code DELETED} addresses are excluded from lists but remain
 * readable by id. The enum is never on the wire.

claims.statement: The status value is never sent on the wire; a read shows a deleted boolean instead.
claims.quote: Soft-deleted addresses expose `deleted: true` on read; the internal `status` enum is not on the wire.

claims.statement: The create and replace request body has the fields name, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode, countryCode, phone, email and roles, all camelCase under their Java names.
claims.quote: Create/update request body. Every field is camelCase on the wire, under its Java name.

claims.statement: A request body that echoes server-assigned fields (id, organisationId, deleted, status, createdAt, modifiedAt) is accepted, and those values are dropped rather than saved.
claims.quote:
Server-assigned fields ({@code id}, {@code organisationId}, {@code deleted}, timestamps) are
 * not components, so a body that echoes them is accepted and they are dropped.
claims.note: The test request_deserialisesFromCamelCaseAndMapsOntoAnEntityIgnoringServerFields sends id, organisationId 'OTHER-ORG', status 'DELETED', deleted true and both timestamps and proves each is null on the entity.

claims.statement: roles is required on create and on update: a missing or empty roles list is refused with 'Select what this address can be used for'.
claims.quote: @NotEmpty(message = "Select what this address can be used for")

claims.statement: A missing roles list is read as an empty list, so it fails the required-roles rule rather than erroring.
claims.quote:
{@code roles} is never null: a missing list reads as empty, and repeated roles collapse to
 * their first occurrence.

claims.statement: A role repeated in the request collapses to its first occurrence, keeping the order the caller sent: CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR becomes CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_ORIGIN.
claims.quote: roles = roles == null ? List.of() : roles.stream().distinct().toList();

claims.statement: Every role in the request must be one of the five role names exactly; an unknown name (such as TRANSPORTER), a lower-case name (such as consignor), a null entry or a blank entry is refused with 'Select valid roles', keyed by roles.
claims.quote: @AddressRoleNames(message = "Select valid roles")

claims.statement: An unknown role name is reported as a field error on roles beside the other field errors, rather than failing the whole body before validation, so every other field error is still shown.
claims.quote: An unknown enum constant would make Jackson throw before validation, which answers as a `bad-request` problem with no `errors` map and hides every other field error. A string component fails Bean Validation, so the `validation-error` problem names `roles` beside the other field errors.
claims.note: mechanism: roles carried as strings in the request and checked by name. The error key is roles, never roles[1].

claims.statement: A request whose only role is unknown gets exactly one violation, on roles: the one-group rule ignores names that are not roles.
claims.quote: It skips role names that are not roles; `@AddressRoleNames` reports those.

claims.statement: There are five address roles: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION, CONSIGNEE and IMPORTER, each a party or a place a notification can choose the address for.
claims.quote: /** A role a notification can choose this address for: a party, or a place. */

claims.statement: The API describes each role: PLACE_OF_ORIGIN 'Where the animals or goods start their journey', CONSIGNOR 'The party sending the consignment', PLACE_OF_DESTINATION 'Where the animals or goods are unloaded in Great Britain', CONSIGNEE 'The party receiving the consignment', IMPORTER 'The party importing the consignment'.
claims.note: The address book holds no display labels for roles; labels are the caller's copy (README Design notes).

claims.statement: Each role belongs to one of two groups: sending (PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR) or receiving (CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION).

| Sending | `PLACE_OF_ORIGIN`, `CONSIGNOR` |
| Receiving | `CONSIGNEE`, `IMPORTER`, `PLACE_OF_DESTINATION` |

role cannot be added without a group. The grouping is internal: it is not part of the API, and a
caller only sees it as a refusal.

claims.statement: The contract states the role rules: at least one roles entry on create and update; roles returned on read, as an empty list when an address has none; a repeated role collapses to its first occurrence; a missing list or unknown value is a 400 keyed by roles with nothing saved; an update replaces the roles; every role must come from one group, sending (PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR) or receiving (CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION); and an address holding any role can be in any country.

**Roles:** at least one `roles` entry is required on create and update, and roles are returned
    on read, as an empty list when an address has none. ... Every role must come from one group: sending
    (PLACE_OF_ORIGIN, CONSIGNOR) or receiving (CONSIGNEE, IMPORTER, PLACE_OF_DESTINATION); a 400
    keyed by `roles` otherwise. An address holding any role can be in any country.
